content: Folic acid is a medication prescribed to treat or prevent a deficiency in folic acid, which is a B-complex vitamin essential for the production of red blood cells. A lack of this vitamin can lead to specific types of anemia, characterized by a low red blood cell count. Folic acid is available in tablet form and is typically taken once daily. It is important to follow the instructions provided on your prescription label carefully. If you have any questions or need clarification, consult your doctor or pharmacist. Take the medication exactly as prescribed, without altering the dose or frequency. If you are using folic acid to address a deficiency, you may notice an improvement in your symptoms quickly, often within 24 hours. However, you should not discontinue the medication unless directed to do so by your doctor. In some cases, folic acid may be prescribed for purposes other than treating a deficiency. If you have questions about these additional uses, consult your doctor or pharmacist for more information. Before starting folic acid, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you have any allergies to folic acid or other medications. Additionally, provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially if you are using phenytoin (Dilantin) or other vitamins. Your doctor may recommend dietary changes to increase your intake of folic acid. Foods such as liver, products made from dried yeast, fruits, and fresh leafy green vegetables are good sources of this vitamin. If you miss a dose of folic acid, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Folic acid may cause side effects. If you experience symptoms such as a skin rash, itching, redness, or difficulty breathing, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program, either online or by phone. Store folic acid in its original container, ensuring it is tightly closed and kept out of reach of children. The medication should be stored at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture, and should not be kept in the bathroom. Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about disposal. In the event of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911 immediately. It is important to keep all appointments with your doctor and any laboratory tests they may order to monitor your response to folic acid. Do not share this medication with others, and consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. Folic acid is also available under the brand name Folvite®.
